root_cause.text: The code dereferences `bs->cur->bc_ops` to check the btree type after `bs->cur` may have become a dangling pointer because it aliases `bs->sc->sa.{bno,rmap}_cur`, which were freed earlier during the scrub operation, leading to a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states "We cannot dereference bs->cur when trying to determine if bs->cur aliases bs->sc->sa.{bno,rmap}_cur after the latter has been freed." The patch moves the `xfs_btree_is_bno` and `xfs_btree_is_rmap` calls to before any potential freeing of the aliased cursors, preserving the correct temporal ordering.

intent_record.how: The change enables runtime identification of whether the current btree cursor operates on the block allocation btree (bnobt) or the reverse mapping btree (rmapbt). intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid NULL pointer dereference by evaluating cursor type flags before possibly nullifying the cursor pointer.

intent_record.how: The conditions now use precomputed booleans that are evaluated before bs->cur may be set to NULL, thereby avoiding a use-after-null situation where bs->cur->bc_ops could be accessed after bs->cur is nullified.
